headlines.title: Why Wall Street’s Breakup Fantasy Doesn’t Work for Netflix
headlines.summary: Breaking up a $326 billion streaming giant sounds straightforward until you try to draw the lines. Netflix's financials reveal a business so deliberately tangled that carving out its studio, ads, live events, or games would leave each piece missing the one thing that makes it worth anything.

headlines.title: Is Netflix Stock More Likely to Hit $100 or $60 by the End of 2026?
headlines.summary: The streaming stock is down 38% in the past 12 months, and its valuation may look enticing to many investors.

headlines.title: Netflix Has Momentum Despite Being Down in 2026. One Analyst’s Price Target Implies 70% Upside
headlines.summary: Netflix has shed more than a third of its value while the broader market climbs, yet one Wall Street analyst sees a path back that would leave today's sellers deeply regretting their exits.

headlines.title: Netflix Has No Dividend. Here's Why Long-Term Investors Should Own It Anyway.
headlines.summary: Despite its recent headwind, the streaming giant still offers more growth potential than plenty of other tickers categorized as growth stocks.

description: Netflix, Inc. provides entertainment services worldwide. The company offers television (TV) series, documentaries, feature films, games, and live programming across various genres and languages. It also provides members the ability to receive streaming content through a host of internet-connected devices, including TVs, digital video players, TV set-top boxes, and mobile devices. Netflix, Inc. was incorporated in 1997 and is headquartered in Los Gatos, California.
